submission.prose: Policy-call execution adapter. It awaits synchronous or promise-like callbacks, classifies normal values and exceptions through configurable result/error predicates, exposes the classification as a tagged result, and can collapse that result back to return-or-throw semantics. It also centralizes per-call success/failure telemetry; concrete policies retain responsibility for retries, timeouts, fallback, and other control flow.

referent.description: The Executor module and its exported execution-classification API

qualifications: Interpretation of captured TypeScript source; execution and deployment behavior were not independently observed.

children.prose: `invoke()` returns `{success}` for an unfiltered fulfillment, `{value}` for a fulfillment selected as failure, and `{error}` for a selected exception. An unselected exception is reported and rethrown. `returnOrThrow()` reverses the wrapper boundary: throw `{error}`, otherwise return the success or filtered value. The supplied test exercises success, handled-error, and unhandled-error cases.

referent.description: Classification and tagged-result conversion implemented by ExecuteWrapper and returnOrThrow

qualifications: The test is corroborating repository source, not evidence that the suite passed.

children.prose: Success and failure listeners are backed by separate emitters. Timing is skipped when neither has listeners; otherwise elapsed milliseconds come from `performance.now()` when available or Node high-resolution time. Filtered values emit handled failures; selected exceptions emit handled failures; unselected exceptions emit unhandled failures before propagation. `clone()` preserves predicates but creates fresh emitters.

children.prose: Policy factories build wrappers from accumulated predicates. Consumers then own policy-specific decisions: RetryPolicy loops over non-success tags and applies backoff/give-up rules; NoopPolicy and TimeoutPolicy invoke once and use `returnOrThrow`, with TimeoutPolicy separately managing cancellation and races. Thus this module normalizes outcomes and telemetry rather than implementing resilience strategies.

referent.description: Delegation between Executor and policy construction/consumers

qualifications: Representative consumers were inspected; other established consumers were not read because they add little to this division-of-responsibility account.
